title: Compose text transformations at run time

blocks.text: Composition does not need a class per behaviour: a class can hold functional interfaces and combine them at run time. The page's `TextProcessor` holds a list of `Function<String, String>` and applies them one after another:

items: `addTransformation(t)` adds `t` after the transformations already added, and returns the same processor every time, so calls chain; trim then upper-case turns `"  hello  "` into `"HELLO"`;
`process(input)` applies the transformations **in the order they were added**: the example above gives `"HELLO_WORLD"`. A transformation added twice runs twice, in each of its places;
a processor with no transformations returns its input unchanged;
the composition is live: a transformation added after `process` has run is used by the next `process` call.

cases.says: Trim then upper-case turns "  hello  " into "HELLO", and addTransformation returns the processor.
trim, upper-case, then spaces to underscores turns "  hello world  " into "HELLO_WORLD".
A processor with no transformations returns "as it is" unchanged.
A transformation added after a process call is applied by the next process call.

concepts: Behaviour composed from functional interfaces can be combined, ordered and extended at runtime without any class hierarchy.
